Cliopatria's Greek City-States keeps Massalia to -43 (eu-01-b).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Massalia (it lies inside Greek City-States -800..83). Both pages give the city only: 'about fifty hectares surrounded by a wall' with 'about 50,000' people at its height (History of Marseille) and no km2 for a territory. The 25 km disc is a reading; the History page says only that natives plotted to destroy the colony (Ligurian conflict, undated).

ledger.note: c. 600: Phocaean Greeks found Massalia. Infobox 'Founded by Greeks from Phocaea: c. 600 BC'; 'Massalia was established c. 600 BC by Ionian Greek settlers from Phocaea, in Western Anatolia'. The History page adds the Carthaginian opposition to the project ('whose fleet was defeated'). The disc of territory is the researcher's reading.
Agathe founded 'late 5th-early 4th c. BC' (year rounded to the century boundary). Location (Agde) is the usual identification; not on the page.

ledger.note: 49: Caesar's siege strips Massalia of its holdings. 'It maintained nominal autonomy but lost its trading empire and was largely brought under Roman dominion'; the Massalia page: 'Massalia lost most of its inland territory in the aftermath of this defeat' (the sentence's 'defeat' is not dated on the page).

ledger.note: 49 (September): Massalia surrenders to Caesar. 'closing its gates to Caesar on his way to Spain in April of 49 BC, the city was besieged'; 'Massalia's fleet was defeated and the city fell by September.' Infobox 'Conquered by Julius Caesar: 49 BC'.

wars.name: Siege of Massilia

zones.text: Massalia and its territory (25 km disc round Marseille, about 1,000 km2)

wars.outcome: The city was besieged from April 49 and fell by September to Caesar's army; it kept nominal autonomy but lost its trading empire.

wars.name: Allobroges and Arverni invasion (123 BC)
wars.outcome: 'In 123 BC, Massalia was faced by an invasion of the Allobroges and Arverni under Bituitus'; Massalia yielded 'a strip of land through its territory which was used to construct the Via Domitia' and 'the Romans organized their province of Transalpine Gaul around it'.
wars.note: The page gives no extent for the strip, so no loss event is drawn; only 123 is on the page (the end year of the Roman intervention is not given).

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier of Massalia; its holdings are a city and coastal colonies.

notes: Thin by page. Neither page gives an area for Massalia's territory (a 50 ha city and 'about 50,000' people) or the location of its colonies; modern names (Agde, Hyères, Antibes, Nice) are the usual identifications, flagged as such. The Via Domitia land strip of 123-121 and the loss of 'most of its inland territory' are not drawn (no extent). Not on the pages opened: the Battle of Alalia, Emporion and Rhode, the wars with the Salyes, the 154 BC Roman aid. Gazetteer names used that it lacks: Agde, Antibes, Hyères (places). The Massalia page puts Massalia 'east of the Rhône'. Tauroentium (early 3rd c.) is in the Massalia page but not drawn.
